name: Posture Recovery from Zombie
description: Defending Zombie restores an inside hand and elbow before the knee hug closes. Posture recovery addresses rubber guard rather than a lower-leg lockdown.
summary: Posture recovery against Zombie prevents the arm-clearing pummel, restores an inside elbow and reduces the high-leg posture connection.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Zombie; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Zombie is not a lower-leg lockdown. Whether half guard or closed guard remains depends on a separate leg exchange.

Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (top): What should block their hand-clearing path early?
flashcards.answer: Keep a useful forearm between the bodies so the free hand cannot easily lift yours outside into New York.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside forearm before knee hug shuts

plausible: Wide mat post beyond their hip
Both hands behind their shoulders
trap: Elbow compact, wrist reaches past it

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (top): How should the hand return to the inside?
flashcards.answer: Recover hand and elbow together through available space, rather than leaving the wrist exposed outside a fixed elbow.
flashcards.answer_line: Hand and elbow move inward together

plausible: Hand alone; elbow beyond their knee
Elbow alone, hand still posted wide
trap: Chest up first; leg guides arm

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (top): What should you do if the shoulder is already locked?
flashcards.answer: Early pummel defense requires free movement; when a shoulder lock is loaded, signal and obtain release before trying to posture.
flashcards.answer_line: Tap; obtain release of the arm trap

plausible: Raise chest before seeking release
Wait for high leg to drop, then tap
trap: Tap while still pulling the held arm

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (top): Where should the high-leg connection loosen?
flashcards.answer: Open space at the high-leg connection while keeping head and arm aligned, then recover posture through the slack.
flashcards.answer_line: At hip and thigh before chest rises

plausible: Only between your knees on the mat
Only between fingers and their wrist
trap: Only free ankle; high thigh holds

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (top): When should you withdraw a captured shoulder?
flashcards.answer: Use the slack to retrieve shoulder and elbow before lifting upright, rather than dragging an arm through the enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: High leg opens; arm can move freely

plausible: Other hand first touches their hip
While knee hug still fixes elbow
trap: Hand clear; shoulder in knee hug

flashcards.question: Zombie posture recovery (top): Chest up, their knees still inside: what have you regained?
flashcards.answer: With the upper-body enclosure cleared, you can face the guard from a stable posture; the remaining legs still need assessment.

plausible: Hips already pinned past their knees
Leg-free side pin after head release
trap: Pass complete; only chest grip left

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (top): Which opponent action is this posture recovery countering?
flashcards.answer: Zombie attempts to clear the hand outside and isolate the arm under the knee hug; it is not a calf lockdown.

plausible: Second leg joins after arm isolation
Head-side hand circles from New York
trap: Shin enters chin after neck clears

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (top): What decides whether half guard remains afterward?
flashcards.answer: The arm pummel does not determine the lower-body destination. Check the legs after recovering posture.
flashcards.answer_line: One of your legs is actually trapped

plausible: Your hand has reached the mat
Your head is above their head

defender.name: Posture Recovery from Zombie Defender
defender.description: Posture Recovery from Zombie (defender): Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Zombie; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Zombie is not a lower-leg lockdown. Whether half guard or closed guard remains depends on a separate leg exchange.

Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward. Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.

Cover the cleared arm and close the knee hug as the hand reaches the mat. Once the arm is isolated, maintain that new control instead of repeatedly treating Zombie as a separate leg entanglement. Keep a safe guard and look for another opening when the opponent maintains inside frames.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

If posture control is lost, use a short hip escape behind your shoulder frame to preserve guard retention. Keep that frame between the bodies against a crossface and chest pressure as you return a knee, rather than reaching after the escaping wrist.
key_principles: Keep Mission Control: Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel.
Find inside space: Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward.
Move the hand to the mat: Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.
Prevent the return pummel: Cover the cleared arm and close the knee hug as the hand reaches the mat.
Recognize New York: Once the arm is isolated, maintain that new control instead of repeatedly treating Zombie as a separate leg entanglement.
Reset a blocked attempt: Keep a safe guard and look for another opening when the opponent maintains inside frames.

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (bottom): What must your high leg do while the free hand pummels?
flashcards.answer: The high Mission Control connection supports the pummel; letting posture escape removes the base for arm isolation.
flashcards.answer_line: Hold posture low with knee supported

plausible: Hang loose as their posture rises
Ankle high with knee drifting back
trap: Free leg grip so both hands pummel

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (bottom): In the hand-first pummel, where is the opening?
flashcards.answer: Eddy's demonstrated option attacks beneath the hand rather than forcing the strongly clamped elbow open.
flashcards.answer_line: Beneath hand, away from elbow clamp

plausible: Beneath the tightest elbow clamp
Over wrist, pressing down on chest
trap: Hook wrist from its outer side

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (bottom): What should you move to clear the inside frame?
flashcards.answer: Guide the whole wrist-and-forearm line toward the mat instead of pulling individual fingers or forcing a fixed elbow.
flashcards.answer_line: Guide wrist and forearm through gap

plausible: Elbow out; hand stays at chest
Hand up; forearm still across chest
trap: Wrist inward to your chest center

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (bottom): What closes the gap after their hand reaches the mat?
flashcards.answer: Follow the hand clearance by wrapping the isolated arm and hugging the supported knee so the hand cannot simply return inside.
flashcards.answer_line: Covering the arm with the knee hug

plausible: Pummeling hand points straight up
Let knee float away from the arm
trap: Wrist held out; elbow left uncovered

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Zombie (bottom): If their posture escapes completely, what should you recover?
flashcards.answer: When the upper-body connection is lost, release the failing high leg and recover ordinary guard behind the frame.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside shoulder frame and knee room

plausible: Same high ankle grip, knee unbraced
Wrist grip as chest fills torso gap
trap: Regrip high leg before near knee in
